newsitem.title: JAPAN: TIFFE Euroyen up on hedge fund buying, tankan.
newsitem.headline: TIFFE Euroyen up on hedge fund buying, tankan.

text.p: The key March Euroyen futures contract on TIFFE was up on Tuesday due to aggressive buying by a U.S. speculator in Singapore and to various market rumours about possible weakness in the Bank of Japan's (BOJ) quarterly "tankan" corporate sentiment survey due on Wednesday.
"In early trade, a U.S. hedge fund bought a significant amount of Euroyen futures on SIMEX though an investment bank, driving up March to a high of 98.96," said a European bank trader.
The March was at 99.93 at midday, up sharply from 98.87 on Monday. Turnover was 40,903 contracts.
There was widespread talk that a senior BOJ official implied in a meeting with some Japanese bank managers on Monday that the tankan would show weak results.
The talk accelerated buying of Euroyen contracts which were already buoyed by the hedge fund's purchases, traders said.

Euroyen futures and JGBs also benefited from talk that JP Morgan revised down a previously optimistic forecast for the tankan, traders said. But JP Morgan's chief economist in Tokyo, Jesper Koll, said on Tuesday that he had not revised a forecast of plus four for the manufacturers' diffusion index.
Forecasts by economists polled by Reuters ranged from minus four to plus four for the June diffusion index (DI) for major manufacturers, and from minus three to minus 10 for major non-manufacturers.
The BOJ refrained from its regular money market operation at 0020 GMT, leaving the market with a projected surplus of 120 billion yen.
